enso.rule: CPC official RONI of the winter the lead window covers: strong El Nino if NDJ or DJF >= 1.5, El Nino if >= 0.5, La Nina if NDJ or DJF <= -0.5

na: SEAS5 expects the Pacific trough regime on 64% of November days against 25% in its own climate (more often; members 59–69%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.68, 90% interval 0.51 to 0.81, p 0.000, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific ridge regime on 2% of November days against 25% in its own climate (less often; members 1–4%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.83, 90% interval 0.71 to 0.91, p 0.000, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific trough regime on 50% of NDJ days against 27% in its own climate (more often; members 46–53%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.41, 90% interval 0.19 to 0.60, p 0.006, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific ridge regime on 4% of NDJ days against 24% in its own climate (less often; members 3–6%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.58, 90% interval 0.36 to 0.75, p 0.000, passes the false-discovery test).
In the hindcast's 14 El Niño winters the Pacific trough regime was observed +8 points in DJF (significant), and SEAS5 predicted +5 — same sign, also significant.
In the hindcast's 14 El Niño winters the Pacific ridge regime was observed -9 points in JFM (significant), and SEAS5 predicted -10 — same sign, also significant.
ea: SEAS5 expects the NAO− / Greenland blocking regime on 36% of December days against 19% in its own climate (more often; members 30–42%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.35, 90% interval 0.12 to 0.54, p 0.021, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the NAO+ regime on 16% of November days against 27% in its own climate (less often; members 12–20%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.55, 90% interval 0.36 to 0.71, p 0.001, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the NAO− / Greenland blocking regime on 29% of NDJ days against 19% in its own climate (more often; members 25–32%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.32, 90% interval 0.07 to 0.55, p 0.031, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Atlantic ridge regime on 30% of November days against 21% in its own climate (more often; members 27–33%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.77, 90% interval 0.56 to 0.89, p 0.000, passes the false-discovery test).

Where the hindcast is skilful its shifts are too small for that skill: median ratio of predictable components 1.3 over those 13 cells (1 = a well-sized signal), so the observed shift is typically larger than the forecast one — read the sign, not the size.
